# QuotaBird

> QuotaBird is a free set of quota, pipeline and comp-plan calculators for B2B sellers and sales managers at cloud providers and SaaS companies, built by Mark Flournoy, who spent six years leading federal partner sales teams at Amazon. 19 one-minute tools for the number they gave you and what they will pay you for it, plus short Field Notes, printable Field Kits and a methodology page that labels every benchmark as published data, a rule of thumb, or a QuotaBird working range.

The tools are plain web pages. Each asks five questions (yes / sort of / no) or takes a few numbers, then gives a verdict, the question a manager will ask, and one thing to do first. The math runs in the browser and nothing typed is sent anywhere; base, variable and quota can be remembered in the visitor's own browser so other tools can prefill them. Shared results are encoded in the URL fragment; no accounts, no uploads, no AI. Privacy: https://quotabird.com/privacy/

## Your number

- [Quota Check](https://quotabird.com/quota/): Your quota against your on-target earnings, judged by what the number is measured in: new bookings, cloud consumption growth, or a whole book. (the day the number lands.)
- [Quota Case](https://quotabird.com/quota-case/): Find the gap between last year and this year's quota: run rate or ARR, pipeline at your real win rate, headcount, one-time deals. Then push back with it, or close it with growth in existing accounts and net-new ones. (when you need to push back.)
- [Territory Check](https://quotabird.com/territory/): Can the territory make the number, or are you being asked to grow where nobody could? Five questions for sellers. (month one in a new territory.)
- [Discount Check](https://quotabird.com/discount/): How much discount is too much? See what it costs in your commission and the company's margin before you say yes. (when they ask you to sharpen the pencil.)

## Your pay

- [Pay Check](https://quotabird.com/pay/): Base, variable, accelerator, cap and threshold in. What the plan pays at 50% to 200% of quota out, and where the upside goes. (when you want to know what the plan really pays.)
- [Commission Check](https://quotabird.com/commission/): Deal size, commission rate and your share of the credit in, what you actually take home out, after the share you set aside for taxes. (when it closes.)
- [Comp Plan Check](https://quotabird.com/comp-plan/): Five questions that find the red flags in a sales comp plan: crediting, payout timing, upside, clawbacks and mid-year changes. (before you count on the plan.)
- [Offer Check](https://quotabird.com/offer/): Two sales job offers side by side: base, variable, ramp and guarantee in, year-one cash and a normal year at a realistic attainment out. (when you have two offers.)

## Your team

- [Pipeline Check](https://quotabird.com/pipeline/): Target, pipeline and win rate in, the gap out. 3X is a rule of thumb; your win rate says what you actually need. (quarterly, before the review.)
- [Risk Check](https://quotabird.com/risk/): Coverage says whether you have enough pipeline. This says how fragile it is: concentration, aging, next steps, timing and creation. (when coverage looks fine and you don't trust it.)
- [Rep Check](https://quotabird.com/rep/): Is it the rep, the territory, a skill gap or an effort gap? Five questions for sales managers that look at the territory before the person. (when a rep is worrying you.)
- [Partner Check](https://quotabird.com/partner/): Five questions that separate a real partnership from promises: sourced deals, a named account, an owner who gets paid, a plan with dates, and pull. (before you renew the partnership.)
- [Talent Review](https://quotabird.com/olr/): Five questions that test the assessment you're making for a rep in a talent review (OLR, at Amazon), then the room pressure-tests you. (review season.)

## Your deal

- [Deal Check](https://quotabird.com/deal/): Five questions (customer, money, power, path, now) that separate proof from hopium in a federal deal. (before you put it in commit.)
- [Account Check](https://quotabird.com/account/): Five questions that tell you whether you know the account or only the opportunity in front of you: mission, money, power, incumbents, how they buy. (when you only know one person there.)
- [Commit Check](https://quotabird.com/commit/): For cloud and consumption sellers: will the customer use their committed spend? See the pace, the monthly spend it takes from here, and the shortfall or overage. (when a commit might not burn.)
- [Federal Readiness Check](https://quotabird.com/federal-readiness/): Five skeptical questions on whether a company has a real federal business: customer, money, buying path, partners and team. (before you bet on federal.)
- [Competition Check](https://quotabird.com/competition/): Five questions that tell you whether the incumbent, the competitor, or doing nothing is beating you right now. (when you're not sure you're ahead.)

## Any meeting

- [Brief Check](https://quotabird.com/brief/): Five questions about the doc, deck or QBR you're about to present, then the room pressure-tests you. (when someone in the room can say no.)

## Methodology and benchmarks

- [How QuotaBird's numbers work](https://quotabird.com/methodology/): where every range and benchmark on QuotaBird comes from, labelled as published data, a common rule of thumb, or a QuotaBird working range. Quota-to-OTE working ranges: bookings 4 to 6x (built on Bridge Group 2026 median 4.6x, 158 B2B companies), run rate or consumption growth 15 to 30x, whole book 40 to 80x (QuotaBird working ranges, derived from quota / OTE = variable share / commission rate). Includes each tool's formula and a last-reviewed date.
- [Quota by the numbers](https://quotabird.com/quota-by-the-numbers/): sourced quota and compensation benchmarks: attainment, median quota and OTE, pay mix, ramp, over-assignment, accelerators.

## Free printable

- [The Manager's Field Kit](https://quotabird.com/kit/): a free, printable field kit for sales managers: how your team's number got built, fighting the plan without losing, handing down a tough quota and still crushing it, inheriting a team, one-on-ones, the forecast call, pipeline, managing up, a struggling rep, review season, managing high performers, and nine worksheets.
- [The Seller's Field Kit](https://quotabird.com/seller/): a free, printable field kit for sellers: where your quota came from, checking it and pushing back, crushing a tough number anyway, is it a real deal, pipeline math, one deal carrying the quarter, single-threaded accounts, discounts, quiet deals, falling behind, and keeping your manager informed.
- [The Leadership Field Kit](https://quotabird.com/leader/): a free, printable field kit for managers who want their influence to travel beyond their team: shaping the number before it shapes your team, what to be known for, a point of view, receipts, templates others can borrow, the right rooms, and developing the people behind you.

## Sales Math Library

- [How much pipeline do you actually need?](https://quotabird.com/math/pipeline-coverage/): Required pipeline coverage is 1 ÷ your qualified win rate. A 3X coverage ratio assumes a 33% win rate; at 20% you need 5X, at 25% you need 4X.
- [What your quota-to-OTE ratio really says](https://quotabird.com/math/quota-to-ote/): Quota ÷ OTE equals your variable share of OTE divided by your commission rate at 100% attainment. SaaS new-bookings plans cluster around 4×; cloud consumption plans, paid at a low single-digit percentage, run far higher by design.
- [What a discount really costs you and the company](https://quotabird.com/math/discount-math/): A discount cuts your commission by exactly the discount percentage, and cuts gross margin to 1 − (1 − margin) ÷ (1 − discount). A 15% discount on a 40% margin leaves about 29%, not 25%.
- [Why your commission check is smaller than the math](https://quotabird.com/math/commission-take-home/): US employers may withhold federal income tax on separately paid commissions at a flat 22% (37% on supplemental wages above $1 million in a year), plus 7.65% Social Security and Medicare, before any state tax. That's withholding, not the tax you finally owe.

## Field Notes

- [Your quota is crazy. Now prove it.](https://quotabird.com/notes/prove-the-quota-is-crazy/): Saying it feels too high has never moved a number. Math sometimes does.
- [How to review an offer, and push back on it](https://quotabird.com/notes/review-an-offer/): The offer letter tells you what they'll pay if everything goes right. Find out what you'll make in a normal year.
- [You think the company is shorting you](https://quotabird.com/notes/think-youre-being-shorted/): Start with the math, then the paperwork, then the right person. In that order.
- [How to explain a bad comp plan without losing the room](https://quotabird.com/notes/explain-a-bad-comp-plan/): You'll roll out a plan you wouldn't have written. Your team will find the ugly parts fast, so get there first.
- [How to fight a comp plan before it ships](https://quotabird.com/notes/fight-a-comp-plan-before-it-ships/): Once the plan ships, you're mostly explaining it. The time to change it is while it's still a draft.
- [OTE is what you make if everything goes right](https://quotabird.com/notes/ote-if-everything-goes-right/): It's a real number. It's the number for a year that goes to plan, and most years don't.
- [Your accelerator only matters if somebody reaches it](https://quotabird.com/notes/accelerators-need-someone-to-reach-them/): A 2× accelerator sounds great in the offer. It pays nothing in a year you finish at 90%.
- [A cap tells you how much upside they're willing to share](https://quotabird.com/notes/what-a-cap-tells-you/): Past the cap, your check stops growing. Where they put it tells you a lot.
- [How a $1M deal turns into a small paycheck](https://quotabird.com/notes/split-credit/): You close a $1M deal. Then the credit rules run.
- [The plan says uncapped. Read the footnotes.](https://quotabird.com/notes/uncapped-read-the-footnotes/): A plan can be uncapped on page one and still limit a big year. Find out before you're counting on one.
- [Weighted pipeline is only as good as the weights](https://quotabird.com/notes/weighted-pipeline/): Your CRM's stage probabilities are numbers somebody typed in once. Check them against what you actually win.
- [You're the rep and the number is crazy](https://quotabird.com/notes/push-back-as-a-rep/): You don't set the number. You can still make a case, if you bring the right one.
- [You have to hand down a number you don't love](https://quotabird.com/notes/handing-down-a-tough-quota/): You made your case upstairs. It didn't move. Now your team needs to hear it from you.
- [The number isn't changing. Now what?](https://quotabird.com/notes/the-number-isnt-changing/): You made the case. It didn't move. Fine. Now figure out what it takes.
- [Before you decide the comp plan sucks, figure out how it pays](https://quotabird.com/notes/read-your-comp-plan/): Most reps read the quota and the OTE and stop. The money is in the rest of it.
- [3X is really a win rate](https://quotabird.com/notes/3x-is-a-win-rate/): Everybody plans to it. Almost nobody asks where it came from.
- [Why I don't start with BANT or MEDDIC](https://quotabird.com/notes/why-not-bant-or-meddic/): They're useful when you're working a deal. The trouble is the moment before that.
- [If three people failed in the same territory](https://quotabird.com/notes/three-people-same-patch/): You probably don't have three bad reps.
- [Your quota went up 30%. Did your territory?](https://quotabird.com/notes/quota-went-up-did-your-territory/): The number moved. Ask what else did.
- [They asked for 15% off. What are you buying with it?](https://quotabird.com/notes/fifteen-percent-off/): A discount is a purchase. The only question is what you got for it.
- [Your best rep hates internal meetings. Is that a problem?](https://quotabird.com/notes/best-rep-hates-meetings/): Probably not the one you think.
